recording.arm: full NEXUS (all four specialists, recovery switched off)
recording.note: A real investigation, copied unchanged from the backend store.

incident.description: A configuration value is invalid (DB_POOL_SIZE=0), causing every /orders and /orders/{id} request to fail deterministically.

database_agent.interpretation: I'll investigate the database health to check for evidence related to this claim.The database itself looks healthy: the `orders` table has 10 rows with a normal status spread (6 completed, 3 pending, 1 failed), and no query failures or performance issues are recorded. The tool returns zero recent queries and a 0.0 ms average, so it provides no evidence of connection-pool exhaustion or the claimed per-request failures — the reported DB_POOL_SIZE=0 issue is not observable from these stats.

changes.description: Increased DB connection pool size placeholder for future load.
changes.author: deepu

changes.description: Initial release of nexus-production simulated service.
changes.author: deepu

change_analysis_agent.interpretation:
I'll investigate the recent deployment history to find changes that could explain this.The only config-type change in the history is chg-002 (v1.0.1, 2026-09-14), described as "Increased DB connection pool size placeholder for future load" — a DB pool size change, which directly matches the DB_POOL_SIZE=0 symptom affecting /orders endpoints. The other two entries are deployments adding endpoints and the initial release, which don't touch DB pool configuration.

Most likely related: **chg-002** ("Increased DB connection pool size placeholder for future load"), the sole DB-pool-related config change — the "placeholder" wording is consistent with an invalid/unset value like DB_POOL_SIZE=0 landing in production.

metrics_agent.interpretation: I'll gather the real metrics before interpreting.Both /orders and /orders/1 show 15/15 requests failing (100% error rate) with very low latency (avg 0.47ms and 0.44ms, p99 under 1ms) — the fast, deterministic failure pattern consistent with a broken config rather than a timeout or load issue. All other endpoints (/health, /db/diagnostics, /changes) show 0 errors with normal 1–1.4ms latencies, so the fault is isolated to the orders paths.

logs_traces_agent.observation: query_logs({'level': 'ERROR', 'limit': 50}) -> ok=True, fields=['entries', 'count']; get_trace({'limit': 20}) -> ok=True, fields=['traces']
logs_traces_agent.interpretation: I'll investigate the logs and traces for evidence of this.The logs confirm the hypothesis: all 30 recent ERROR entries are `GET /orders` and `GET /orders/{id}` returning HTTP 500 with the exact message `"ConfigError: DB_POOL_SIZE must be > 0, got 0"`, all at the same instant (2026-10-13T18:20:56Z) with sub-millisecond durations (0.35–0.8 ms), indicating immediate failure before any real work — consistent with a deterministic config-validation failure rather than a runtime dependency timeout. Meanwhile other endpoints (`/health`, `/metrics`, `/logs`, `/changes`, `/db/diagnostics`) return 200, so the fault is isolated to the orders routes.

hypotheses.statement: The root cause is a configuration error: DB_POOL_SIZE is set to 0 (invalid, must be > 0), causing GET /orders and GET /orders/{id} to fail immediately with HTTP 500 ConfigError, while other endpoints remain healthy.
missing_evidence: The actual configuration values/effective config for DB_POOL_SIZE at runtime
A config diff or deployment log showing DB_POOL_SIZE being set to 0
Timeline correlating the onset of errors with when DB_POOL_SIZE was changed to 0
hypotheses.requested_next_investigation: Inspect current configuration settings (DB_POOL_SIZE) and the change/config history that set it to 0

hypotheses.statement: Change chg-002 (config v1.0.1, 2026-09-14, 'Increased DB connection pool size placeholder for future load') introduced or corresponds to the invalid DB_POOL_SIZE=0 value that breaks the orders endpoints.
missing_evidence: The exact config delta of chg-002 showing the DB_POOL_SIZE value it set
Timestamp evidence linking the onset of the /orders errors to chg-002 rather than a later undocumented change
hypotheses.requested_next_investigation: Retrieve the configuration diff and value for chg-002 to confirm it set DB_POOL_SIZE=0

unsupported_assumptions: That DB_POOL_SIZE was *changed* by a deployment/config change; the change history (ev-3957a18c after chg-002 only *increased* pool size) shows no change that set it to 0, so the 'configuration error' origin (typo, default, env override) is unproven.
That the failing requests depend on the DB pool while /db/diagnostics does not is assumed from endpoint-pairing; the error text is the only direct linkage.
alternative_explanations: DB_POOL_SIZE=0 is present in effective runtime config from an out-of-band env var/secret override rather than a tracked change; still a config error but a different provenance than the change history implies.

The ConfigError could be raised by a validation path that is only reached by the orders handlers (e.g. they check pool size eagerly), meaning the 'root cause' is code-path validation rather than a genuinely unusable pool.
requested_evidence: Effective runtime configuration values (current config snapshot) for DB_POOL_SIZE to directly confirm it is 0 at runtime
Any config-change record or deployment log entry (beyond chg-001/002/003) that set DB_POOL_SIZE to 0, with its timestamp, to establish onset/regression timeline
critic_results.rationale: The error log ev-99d6ea66 shows 30/30 failures on /orders and /orders/1 with the exact message 'ConfigError: DB_POOL_SIZE must be > 0, got 0', and ev-404db9ef confirms those two endpoints carry all 30 errors while /health, /db/diagnostics, /changes succeed with 200s, matching the predicted scope; no evidence_pool item contradicts the statement and orders data exists (ev-2abb4ca4), so the stated fault is genuinely supported. The only gap is provenance of the invalid value (no tracked change set it to 0, per ev-3957a18c), which is a missing-detail caveat, not a contradiction.
